reverseDependencyCheck.claim: AIBT.Runtime and AIBT.Authoring never reference AIBT.Editor
reverseDependencyCheck.result: confirmed -- neither asmdef's references array contains "AIBT.Editor"; the detached-harness compile (this gate's step 3) independently proves this, since AIBT.Editor is Editor-platform-only and any accidental reverse reference from Runtime/Authoring would have failed to compile in a project where Editor-only code is unavailable outside the Editor platform context.

method: Enumerated every .asmdef under Runtime/, Authoring/, and Editor/ (3 total; P1/P2-GATE covered only the first two since Editor/ barely existed before Phase 3), confirmed their references contain none of the forbidden categories beyond what AIBT.Editor's own asmdef already declares (includePlatforms: ["Editor"] is the only Editor-specific surface, and it references no MCP or LLM-provider assembly), and confirmed no source file under Runtime/ or Authoring/ imports UnityEditor, Unity.Entities, or an MCP/LLM-provider namespace (grep for 'using UnityEditor', 'Unity.Entities', 'UnityMCP', 'OpenAI', 'Anthropic' across Runtime/ and Authoring/ returned no matches). The detached-harness compile independently proves the reference direction: since the harness project resolves AIBT.Runtime/AIBT.Authoring exactly as declared, any undeclared or reversed reference would have failed to compile rather than merely being unobserved.

newAssemblyReferencesAddedDuringPhase3.decision: escalated via AskUserQuestion before implementation; accepted -- reuses the same package/pattern AIBT.Authoring.CanonicalTreeJson already establishes for *.aibt.json, applied to *.aibt.layout.json

not escalated as a new architectural boundary -- Unity.Collections is a data-only dependency (NativeArray<T>.ReadOnly) needed to read P3-010's already-public native trace-channel types; no InternalsVisibleTo or forbidden-category dependency was introduced
